implementation.cleanup: caller-side, zero bytes, observed as the bare C3 at 0x00e7b7b1. observed_mechanics: 0x00e7b630 SUB ESP,0x8 -- the only frame instruction. It makes ESP eight bytes below the entry stack pointer and both halves of the reservation are used, at different times.
0x00e7b633 CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0x112],0x1 -- the first of five single-byte guards. Two compare against 1 and three against BL, which is zero. ESI is read seven times and written NEVER.
0x00e7b63a PUSH EBP / 0x00e7b63b MOV EBP,[ESP+0x10] -- EBP is loaded from the ONE ordinary stack argument, not from a frame pointer; there is no MOV EBP,ESP anywhere in the 386 bytes.
0x00e7b63f and 0x00e7b64c JZ 0x00e7b7ad -- the two early exits that skip everything. Both land on the POP EBP, with exactly one word outstanding, and neither has run the PUSH EBX or the PUSH EDI.
0x00e7b652 PUSH EBX / 0x00e7b653 XOR EBX,EBX -- EBX becomes a zero constant and the only register the body writes other than the frame and the calls.
0x00e7b65b, 0x00e7b667 and 0x00e7b673 JNZ 0x00e7b7ac -- the other three early exits. All three land on the POP EBX, with two words outstanding, and none of them reaches the POP EDI.
0x00e7b66d CMP byte ptr [EBP + 0x17b],BL -- the fifth guard, and the only displacement the body reaches through the value it loaded from the stack.
0x00e7b679 MOV EAX,[ESI] -- the body's incoming EAX is overwritten before it is ever read, so the machine never reads it; the model test supplies one anyway so the entry shape is complete.

0x00e7b67b MOV ECX,[0x016b3c04] / 0x00e7b682 ADD ECX,0x1c / 0x00e7b686 CALL 0x00b72210 -- the first call: a hidden register in ECX and one stack word, which the callee pops (RET 0x4, read from the image at 0x00b7221f). This is the only callee-popped word pair that balances the frame.

0x00e7b68b MOV ECX,[EAX+0x1b0] / 0x00e7b691 PUSH ECX -- THE INSTRUCTION PAIR THAT DECIDES THE RECEIVER. ECX is loaded out of memory and passed on as an ordinary stack argument; it is never dereferenced, which is why the machine record abstains with ecx_read_without_deref and why this package claims no receiver.

0x00e7b696 CALL 0x00e6d200 -- four stack words, in push order: ECX, 0x31, 0 (EBX), and the EAX just returned. The caller drops all four with ADD ESP,0x10 at 0x00e7b6a7, so at this call site the callee leaves the stack where it found it.

0x00e7b69b FSTP dword ptr [ESP + 0x20] -- pops an x87 register this body never pushed and stores it at S-4, the float local. The value is whatever ST0 held on entry to 0x00e6d200, which the evidence does not determine.

0x00e7b6ad CALL 0x00b72160 -- no stack word; its EAX is the base the record fill runs through. 0x00b72160's own body was read and it is a pool allocator: 47 instructions, plain RET, and it computes an element address from a base, a stride and a free list.
0x00e7b6bc CALL 0x00b72210 -- the call the target VA sits inside. One stack word, RET 0x4, and its EAX is the record base.

0x00e7b6c1 FLD dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] -- reads the S-4 float local back, at a different stack-pointer value (S-20 rather than S-36) and with a different displacement (0x10 rather than 0x20). Same slot, twice; the model test derives both from its own walk.
0x00e7b6c5 XORPS XMM0,XMM0 -- the only XMM write, and its two consumers are the MOVSS at 0x00e7b6ea and 0x00e7b6ef.
0x00e7b6c8 FST dword ptr [EAX+0x1c] and 0x00e7b6cb FSTP dword ptr [EAX+0x20] -- FST DOES NOT POP, so both stores take the same register and 0x1c and 0x20 receive the same word.
0x00e7b6ce MOV dword ptr [EAX+0x24],0x20 -- the only immediate the body stores.

0x00e7b6db OR ECX,0xffffffff -- an OR with all ones sets every bit, so the two dwords at 0x30 and 0x34 are 0xffffffff whatever ECX held. That is arithmetic on the instruction, not a guess about the global's value.

0x00e7b74e LEA ECX,[ESP+0xc], 0x00e7b76c LEA EDX,[ESP+0xc] and 0x00e7b7a2 LEA ECX,[ESP+0xc] -- three LEAs of the SAME address, S-8, with the stack pointer at S-20 in all three cases. The slot is zeroed by 0x00743b50 at 0x00e7b761, written by 0x00e4cc40 at 0x00e7b772 and read by 0x00e82130 at 0x00e7b7a6.

0x00e7b755 and 0x00e7b75e MOV byte ptr -- the body's only two single-byte stores, at 0x74 and 0x08. The model test reads the dword at 0x75 and requires it to be 0x00a5a5a5, which is three guard bytes and the low byte of the four-byte store at 0x78; that is the proof that the store at 0x74 covered one byte and not four.
0x00e7b777 MOV ECX,[EAX+0xb8] then 0x00e7b77d PUSH ECX then 0x00e7b77e CALL 0x00e5d7b0 -- the one stack word is read out of whatever 0x00e4cc40 returned, at a displacement of 0xb8.

0x00e7b783 FLDZ then 0x00e7b78d FSTP dword ptr [ESP] -- the sharpest thing in the argument list: the body pushes ECX and then stores +0.0f's bit pattern OVER the third of 0x00e780a0's four stack words.

0x00e7b7ab POP EDI / 0x00e7b7ac POP EBX / 0x00e7b7ad POP EBP -- the epilogue. The three POPs are reached on the fall-through path and, in part, by the two early exits: the JZ target is the POP EBP and the JNZ target is the POP EBX.

0x00e7b7ae ADD ESP,0x8 / 0x00e7b7b1 RET -- the reservation is given back and the body returns without popping anything, which is what the record's cleanup.side=caller and bytes=0 describe and what the model test measures.

CONTROL FLOW. Three basic blocks: the head carrying the two JZ, the body carrying the three JNZ, and the epilogue. Five conditional branches, ten CALLs, no conditional call, no JMP, no LOOP and no indirect transfer of any kind. There is exactly one return site.

THE NINE CALLS, in listing order, with what the body hands each: 0x00b72210 (ECX = [0x016b3c04]+0x1c, one word = [ESI+0], callee pops it); 0x00e6d200 (four words: ECX, 0x31, 0, EAX); 0x00b72160 (ECX = [0x016b3c04]+0x54, no word); 0x00b72210 (ECX = [0x016b3c04]+0x54, one word = the EAX just returned, callee pops it); 0x00743b50 (ECX = S-8, no word, writes 0); 0x00e4cc40 (two words: S-8 and [EBP+0x108]); 0x00e5d7b0 (one word: [EAX+0xb8]); 0x00e780a0 (four words: [EBP+0], 1, ECX, 0 -- and the third is then overwritten with +0.0f); 0x00e59a70 (EAX in, no word); 0x00e82130 (ECX = S-8, no word). Ten CALL sites, nine distinct callees, and 0x00b72210 is called twice.

GLOBALS. Eight distinct data-segment addresses and thirteen loads, and no store through any of them: 0x016b3c04 three times, 0x016b3c28, 0x016b3c2c and 0x016b3c30 twice each, and 0x015a7c4c, 0x015a7c50, 0x015a7c54 and 0x015a7c58 once each. Six of the record's eight global-filled displacements are the same three words twice over. The model test MAP_FIXEDs both .data pages, plants eight recognisable words in them, and requires each to reach the record at the displacement the listing names.

THE RECORD THE BODY FILLS: twenty-six writes to the base EAX, at displacements 0x04, 0x08, 0x1c, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x2c, 0x30, 0x34, 0x38, 0x3c, 0x40, 0x44, 0x48, 0x4c, 0x50, 0x54, 0x58, 0x5c, 0x60, 0x64, 0x68, 0x6c, 0x70, 0x74 and 0x78. Two of them are single-byte. The run 0x0c..0x1b and the word at 0x00 are NOT written by this body. These are DISPLACEMENTS out of instructions: no type, no member, no size and no layout is declared for the base, and what lives there is 0x00b72210's business and is not in evidence.

xrefs. ghidra_function reports xref_count 1, a single reference from 00e7e8f1, and the xref export's ten outgoing rows (knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv lines 159763..159772) are keyed on 00e7b630, the real entry, not on the queue's VA. NO CLASS IS CLAIMED.

VIRTUAL DISPATCH. None. All ten transfers are CALLs with an immediate operand, and the machine dispatch record agrees at indirect_calls 0, vtable_shaped_loads 0 and call_offsets []. 0x00e7b6c0 is in no sound vptr-backed table.
semantic_findings: 0x00e7b6c0 IS NOT A FUNCTION ENTRY. It is offset 0x90 of FUN_00e7b630 and the fourth byte of the rel32 of the direct call at 0x00e7b6bc. The evidence pack's own ghidra_function sub-record says so: entry_point 00e7b630, body_start 00e7b630. Everything this package reconstructs is the 386-byte body, and the queue's VA is carried in the symbol name only because that is the token the validator binds a source span with.

THE MACHINE ABI RECORD ABSTAINS, AND SO DOES THIS PACKAGE -- IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. conventions.calling_convention is null with candidates [__cdecl, __thiscall] and ambiguity receiver_undetermined; the receiver is undetermined with reason ecx_read_without_deref. So no convention token appears in the source, no receiver parameter is declared, and no field, member, object size or layout is claimed for any pointer the body touches. The model test carries the record's own values as data and checks each against a literal written in the test, so a package that quietly reverted to a receiver or a convention claim fails rather than passes.

ECX IS NOT A RECEIVER HERE, and the listing says so before the record does. MOV ECX,[EAX+0x1b0] at 0x00e7b68b is a load OUT of memory; PUSH ECX at 0x00e7b691 passes the loaded value as the first of 0x00e6d200's four ordinary stack arguments. ECX is read and written seventeen times across the body and dereferenced nowhere, and the rest of the body works through EAX, EBX, EDX, EDI, EBP and ESI.

THE MACHINE RECORD IS INCOMPLETE ABOUT THE STACK ARGUMENT, and the reading is given with its own evidence rather than by editing the record. abi_derived.stack_arguments marks entry_ESP+0x4 `read: false` because its linear ESP walk never calibrated the frame (`untrusted_frame_stack_reads: push ebp with no mov ebp,esp`). The frame IS calibratable: SUB ESP,0x8 then PUSH EBP puts the stack pointer at S-12, so [ESP+0x10] is [S+4] = entry_ESP+0x4, and the body reads it. The record's second abstention -- `flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +8, so the listing is not one path` -- is the same fact from the other side: the listing is not one path, because three of its five conditional branches are early exits that never reach the rest.

THE CLEANUP IS CALLER-SIDE AND ZERO BYTES, and that is forced by the body's own arithmetic rather than read off the record. Sixteen pushes, 0x8+0x10+0xc+0x10+0x8 = 0x34 removed by SUB/ADD and three more by the POPs: the body is eight bytes deeper at its RET than at its entry, and the only two callee-popped words in the whole body are 0x00b72210's two RET 0x4s, read out of the image as five instructions ending c2 04 00. Sixteen minus eight is eight, so the RET must pop nothing. The model test re-derives that from the bytes and then MEASURES it through a calibrated indirect-call probe whose controls pop zero, four and eight bytes.

THE FRAME IS EIGHT BYTES AND BOTH HALVES ARE USED, AT DIFFERENT TIMES. S-4 is a 32-bit float local, written by FSTP [ESP+0x20] with the stack pointer at S-36 and read back by FLD [ESP+0x10] with it at S-20. S-8 is a 32-bit handle local whose address is formed three times, always with the stack pointer at S-20, and which 0x00743b50 zeroes, 0x00e4cc40 writes and 0x00e82130 reads. The two locals are at the same eight bytes, and the reuse is only sound because the byte that is live at any moment is the one the listing's next instruction names.

FST DOES NOT POP, and that makes the pair at 0x1c and 0x20 a copy rather than two values. ModRM 0x50 at 0x00e7b6c8 is /0 (FST) and ModRM 0x58 at 0x00e7b6cb is /3 (FSTP). Both stores therefore take the same register -- the value reloaded from the S-4 local -- and the FSTP's pop leaves one x87 register that the body did not push. The model test plants a second, different value in the observer's ST1 and requires neither field to be it, so a transcription that spelled the first store FSTP dies there.

THE FSTP AT 0x00e7b78d OVERWRITES A PUSHED ARGUMENT. The body pushes EBX, then ECX, then stores +0.0f's bit pattern over the ECX slot, then pushes 1 and [EBP+0]. So the THIRD of 0x00e780a0's four stack words is 0x00000000 and not the value in ECX. The model test observes the four words the callee is handed and requires exactly that.

THE RETURN IS void ON THE LISTING'S OWN EVIDENCE, and that is a reading rather than a recovered fact. No instruction places a value in a return register at the single return site. EAX's last write is 0x00e7b79b, whose only consumer is the call that follows it; XMM0's last write is the XORPS, consumed by the two MOVSS. The machine record's ST0/float_or_x87 claim is carried as data and is NOT adopted: the body pushes the x87 stack twice and pops it three times, so whatever ST0 held on entry is consumed and nothing is left. The RT1 rule's stated basis -- that an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body -- is a property of every SSE instruction ever written and not a statement about a return.

TWO CONTRADICTIONS ON THE CALLEE SIDE ARE REPORTED AND NOT RESOLVED. 0x00e6d200's highest-addressed instruction pair is 83 c4 14 c3 and 0x00e780a0's is 83 c4 10 c3, read from the image. Taken at these two call sites those forms would each remove four bytes more than the caller removes, and the epilogue would not close. The exits these sites actually take are therefore not the ones Ghidra reports as those functions' highest-addressed instructions, and this package cannot say which they are. It does not need to: the frame is forced by the body's own arithmetic, which the model test checks independently, and both terminator readings are carried as data and flagged.

THE OBSERVERS ARE HARNESS, NOT CLAIMS. The nine callees are declared in the header and defined in the model test as observers that record what they were handed and reproduce the terminator form the image records. Nothing is claimed about what any of them does beyond the call shape and the stack discipline the listing fixes, with two exceptions the evidence supports: 0x00b72160's own body was read (47 instructions, a pool allocator with a free list, plain RET) and 0x00e823a0's own body was read (23 instructions, *param_2 = param_1 then a refcount increment, plain RET).

blockers.check: SOURCE SPAN (root cause of every NOT_AVAILABLE check)
blockers.detail: The canonical index record for 0x00e7b6c0 has name = null and normalized_symbol = null, so validate._target_span has no raw_name to narrow a function span with and every check that needs the span reads 'target source span is not deterministically available'. Those two fields are filled only from knowledgegraph/research/source-reconstruction-manifest.json (functions[].normalized_symbol) or from the triage queue's name for the VA (tools/reconstruction_knowledge.py:1042-1043); the triage queue carries no name for 0x00e7b6c0 and this VA has no manifest entry. No worker-authored file can supply either field, and both of those inputs belong to the integrator. This is the state the briefing described and it is unchanged by this package: writing the staging package bound the SOURCE (reconstruction/staging/pkg-w2-00e7b6c0/w2_00e7b6c0_entry.cpp is now the report's source with a digest) but not the SPAN.

abi_derived.verdict is ABI_UNKNOWN. If a span bound, validate's ABI arm would be pinned to WARN with the record's own first abstention as its detail whatever the source said; with no span it reads NOT_AVAILABLE. The record resolves no convention (candidates __cdecl and __thiscall, ambiguity receiver_undetermined) and abstains on the receiver, and the only way past that arm would be a convention or receiver claim the evidence does not support.

With no span the check reads NOT_AVAILABLE. Were one to bind it would still not reach PASS: the machine-derived receiver record names NO register (receiver.register is null), so validate has no register to scan the listing under, and the register-agnostic absence arm does not apply either because the body plainly addresses memory (twenty-six writes through EAX, four reads through ESI, three through EBP). Declaring field offsets would not turn NOT_AVAILABLE into a PASS -- it would only move it to WARN -- and would be a layout claim the evidence does not ground, so it is not done. The root cause is the same receiver abstention as ABI's.

With no span the check reads NOT_AVAILABLE. The pack also records missing_sections [DECOMPILATION, 'no persisted or live decompilation for this target'], and the derived return record is at confidence APPROXIMATION under rule RT1.

The export's ten outgoing direct-call rows for this body exist and are keyed on 0x00e7b630, the real function entry, which this target VA is not (knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv lines 159763-159772, callsites 00e7b686..00e7b7a6). Seven of the eight cells (g++ -O0/-O1/-O3, clang++ -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3) build with zero warnings under -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror and run 525 checks with 0 failures, exit 0. The EIGHTH, g++ -O2, builds with zero warnings and then SEGFAULTS inside the model test's own HARNESS, after the third observer call and with the reconstruction's emitted body already byte-verified by case A: objdump on the -O2 object and on the -O2 linked PIE binary both show callee_00b72160 emitted complete (51 / e8 rel32 / 59 / 89 c8 / c3), and the -O2 linked binary's reconstruction body is byte-identical to the image at all 326 literal positions. The observed symptom is that the word the reconstruction pushes for the second 0x00b72210 arrives as 0 rather than as the record base, i.e. EAX out of the 0x00b72160 observer. This is NOT diagnosed and it is NOT worked around. It is reported, not claimed as a pass.

unresolved_questions: What is 0x016b3c04, and what are 0x016b3c28, 0x016b3c2c, 0x016b3c30, 0x015a7c4c, 0x015a7c50, 0x015a7c54 and 0x015a7c58? Thirteen loads and no store; the model test plants words in both pages and checks each reaches the record, but nothing names them.

What is the value at ESI+0x112, +0x113, +0x178, +0x17f, +0, and at the stack argument's +0x00, +0x108 and +0x17b? Five single-byte guards and three dwords are located exactly; what they MEAN is not in evidence.

What is 0x00e6d200's ECX, held in the callee's hidden register, and what does it do? Its own body WAS decompiled (Simulator::Cell::PlayAnimation) but this package claims nothing about it beyond the four stack words the listing pushes and the stack discipline the listing shows.

How many x87 registers does 0x00e6d200 leave, and with what values? The FSTP at 0x00e7b69b pops one this body never pushed, so its value is whatever ST0 held on entry. The model test therefore takes the ST0 content as a PARAMETER and pins only the ORDER of the two stores, which are the same value because FST does not pop.

Why does the xref export carry no outgoing edge for 0x00e7b6c0 when it carries ten for 0x00e7b630? The export appears to be keyed on function entries and this target is not one. Until that is settled the validator's CALLS check compares a source's call set against an empty machine set and cannot reach an agreement.

Which exit does 0x00e6d200 take when called from 0x00e7b696, and which does 0x00e780a0 take when called from 0x00e7b793? Ghidra reports ADD ESP,0x14;RET and ADD ESP,0x10;RET as their highest-addressed instruction pairs, and neither can be the exit these sites take without unbalancing the epilogue.

Is the machine record's ST0/float_or_x87_in_ST0 return claim wrong, or does this body leave a value in ST0 that the listing does not show? The body pops three x87 registers and pushes two, which is the opposite of leaving a return value, and this package adopts void on the listing's own evidence. The divergence is recorded, not resolved.

What is at the base EAX, and what do the twenty-six written displacements mean? Offsets 0x04..0x78 are located, two of the writes are single-byte, and the run 0x0c..0x1b is untouched -- but no type, member, size or layout is claimed, because the base is 0x00b72210's result and nothing in evidence describes it.

Why does the g++ -O2 build of the MODEL TEST segfault inside its own harness while the same sources pass at -O0, -O1, -O3 and under clang++ at every level? The reconstruction's emitted body is byte-identical at -O2 and the failing symbol's machine code is complete in both the object and the linked binary.

What is the relationship between the pool base 0x016b3c04, the record EAX fills, and the object 0x00b72160 allocates from? 0x016b3c04+0x1c and +0x54 are used as hidden registers and 0x00b72160's own body shows a free-list allocator; whether the +0x1c and +0x54 regions are two pools, two generations of one pool, or something else is not in evidence.
